Subject: Kickoff: procurement sequencing & target close window

Hi Tessa —

Thanks for taking this on. Procurement here is looking to lock in a shared timeline so legal can sequence the MSA/DPA and the order form without blocking the pilot start (Sept 20). High-level asks from our side:

- One canonical MAP (mutual action plan) with dates that tie legal milestones to procurement sign-offs.
- A short list of gating docs: executed MSA, executed DPA, signed order form (with PS SOW if needed).
- Lead times for SOC2 and subprocessor evidence so we can schedule our security review.

We attached a draft internal MAP (IvyCare_MAP_v1.xlsx) — it's optimistic. Can Redwood provide a recommended sequencing with clear owners and the minimum acceptable order to start pilot (i.e., can we start on an MFN order form + provisional DPA text while MSA redlines finish?).

Maya will be our day‑to‑day. Let me know if legal at Redwood wants to join a short call tomorrow.

Thanks,
Raj
Head of Procurement
IvyCare Health

Subject: Re: Kickoff: procurement sequencing & target close window

Hi Raj — thanks for the clear ask and the MAP. Quick answers up front:

1) Minimum to start pilot (non-production): signed order form referencing a standard MSA + provisional DPA (NDA already in place), with a follow-up commitment to finalize MSA redlines within 30 days of signature.

2) For production or any PHI-related scope, we need executed MSA + DPA before provisioning private (VPC) resources.

3) SOC2 + subprocessor evidence: we can provide a current SOC2 report and our subprocessor list within 48 hours after your formal NDA triggers (we consider the existing NDA active, but we can reissue a short access letter).

I'm looping in Karthik (legal) and Laura (CS/onboarding) to propose a concrete sequencing and owners. Proposed quick cadence: 20-min sync tomorrow to align the MAP dates, then Redwood will post a suggested MAP in Drive that includes canary/start gates.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Raj / Maya / Tessa —

Thanks. I reviewed the IvyCare MAP and sketched an ordered lane that balances time-to-start with legal protections. Summary (attached as PDF):

- Lane A (Pilot-ready, non-PHI):
  * Day 0: Execute Order Form (minimal terms) pointing to Redwood standard MSA and DPA.
  * Day 0–30: Parallel redline window for MSA. DPA signed or provisional DPA annex to be accepted with an escalation clause.
  * Day 30–45: Final MSA signature; Order Form remains effective retroactively.

- Lane B (Production / PHI / VPC):
  * Must have fully executed MSA + DPA before VPC onboarding.
  * Security evidence (SOC2 + subprocessor docs) required before provisioning; we can time-box access to SOC2 to expedite review.

Open legal items we want to flag now: data residency clause language for EU or specific-state residency (if applicable); indemnity/cap limits linked to order form tiers; and a short SLA annex for Dedicated capacity.

Next steps I propose: 30-min triage call Wednesday 23 Aug 14:00 PT to agree owners and set concrete dates in the MAP. After the call Redwood will upload a redlined MSA/DPA draft and a suggested MAP spreadsheet (I put a working filename: redwood_msa_dpa_redlines_20270823.pdf).

Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference

Thanks everyone — the Wednesday slot worked well for internal stakeholders; quick recap and commitments from our side:

- Procurement will sign a limited order form (Pilot SKU) by Fri 27 Aug provided Redwood posts the provisional DPA text and an MSA redline that preserves liability caps at 3x fees.
- Security will accept SOC2 and subprocessor list by Mon 30 Aug if access to the SOC2 is provided today.
- Legal will fast-track review so that we aim for MSA final by Sep 15 and production provisioning the week of Sep 20.

Can Redwood confirm the owner for the provisional DPA (IvyCare needs a named contact and a copy in Drive) and confirm whether Dedicated capacity requires a separate order form or an addendum to the same order form. Also please upload the MAP with milestone owners (Procurement/Legal/Redwood) so we can put internal reminders into our ticketing system.
